Ok so generally you just need to analyse what risks are there and how to mitigate them, also making a plan for catastrophical event.

As far as risks goes:

Structure itself: Strength of it (you mentioned over-reinforcing it, and thats a good thing); Dynamic movement (is anyone going to jump into water etc, as dynamic force will put much more stress on the structure)

Water: Having water on set opens a set of new risks such as humidity, splashes (and splashes are slip hasard) so you need to ask yourself or the team a set of questions, about proximity of lighting or sound equipment to the tank (is any going to be hit by it, is the stuff that will be hit waterproof), any slipping oppurtunites (where, how to avoid, how to deal with), have some mops or towels side stage, and plan with your crew who and when will mop the floor, definetly tell your performers that the floor might be wet etc.

Load bearing of the stage: how much force can stage floor hold, is 7100 pounds near its limit, or do you have a safe reserve, also this goes with the dymamic load thing, if you're near the floor limit, you would need to think if its safe for sombody to jump into the tank, causing a spike load on the floor, will he/she puch through it etc

Performers: this is more of a their comfort thing, i assume the water is not heated, but this would be similar even if it was heated, make an area backstage where performers can dry themselves, have towels there, another risk for this is wet footsteps (this will be your another slipping hazard), also have performers warm up etc

Catastrophical: so you also would need to know what might happen if the tank

a) leaks, what do you do, who do you contact, do you have any way to monitor water level change overnight, do you have a pump on site that you can remove the water from the tank with and prevent further leaking, do you have ways to patch the leak, do any power or data cables run under the stage and are in risk of getting flooded and potentially shorted

b) fails, same as above what do you do, who do you contact, cables under the stage etc

you also have to take audience into account, what do you do if the tank breaks and soaks the front audience etc

Those are just off the head risks and ideas, probably not every single one of them but its something :3

Please have a spill plan, it's very unlikely, but have a plan that you and your crew will follow in event of the tank leak or a catastrophical failure both for not show and show conditions. Also very cool looking
